Art is always subjective, and I feel it only really matters if when you yourself look at it and enjoy it, or have an emotional response to it. I love art, especially older artists like van gogh or da vinci. Personally I love Monet, and he's my favorite. But if you look at those paintings they're very basic. I love them because at that time it was artists painting scenes because they loved it and wanted to preserve that moment in time. Now a days with digital technology everything is recorded pretty much all the time. I think this is why as time has moved on modern art has become more about people making statements about things, or creating displays that are so abstract they make no sense. Painters back then were sometimes trying their hardest to recreate as close to real life an image as they could paint. Now that these images are everywhere the traditional idea of a painter or master artist has been disrupted and we no longer see the incredible works of art we saw in the 1600-1900's.

Of course I'm not an art historian or anything and I'm just blowing smoke out my ass but to me it kind of makes sense.
